prompt.v: △ABC is equilateral, with AB = 10x − 22 and BC = 9x − 17. What is x?

problems.text: equilateral: AB 10x - 22, BC 9x - 17; find x
problems.explain: Every side of an equilateral triangle is the same length, so 10x − 22 = 9x − 17. Take 9x from both sides: x − 22 = −17; add 22: x = 5. Check: both sides come to 28. So x = 5.

prompt.v: △ABC is equilateral, with AB = 2x + 13 and CA = 3x + 2. What is x?

problems.text: equilateral: AB 2x + 13, CA 3x + 2; find x
problems.explain: Every side of an equilateral triangle is the same length, so 2x + 13 = 3x + 2. Take 2x from both sides: x + 2 = 13; take away 2: x = 11. Check: both sides come to 35. So x = 11.

prompt.v: △ABC is equilateral, with AB = 2x − 3 and BC = 4x − 13. How long is each side?

problems.text: equilateral: AB 2x - 3, BC 4x - 13; find side
problems.explain: Every side of an equilateral triangle is the same length, so 2x − 3 = 4x − 13. Take 2x from both sides: 2x − 13 = −3; add 13: 2x = 10; divide by 2: x = 5. Then each side is 2(5) − 3 = 7. (x is not the answer: put it back in.) So each side is 7.

problems.explain: The order of the letters is the matching: A↔Z, B↔X, C↔Y. So CA matches YZ, and corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal: 10x − 37 = 2x + 3. Take 2x from both sides: 8x − 37 = 3; add 37: 8x = 40; divide by 8: x = 5. Check: both come to 13. (XY matches BC, not CA.) So x = 5.
